Latin word

restō

restō, restāre, restitī

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

be left, remain

In this lexicon

  • remain

    the recommended word · classical · Cato Agr. 2.1: quid restet; Cic. Sen. 46: quī paucī admodum restant; Traupman 370

Notes

  1. 1restō: short e (Lewis & Short rē-sto). A compound of stō and the prefix re- (de Vaan 516, s.v. re-, red-). Lewis & Short writes rē- before sc, sp and st, and only there. Its article on the prefix gives rĕ, with a by-form rĕd-, and puts the poets’ rēdūcō, rēlātum down to “the suppression of the d”; the long mark before s and a consonant seems to rest on the same idea, as its dī-scindō from dis- does. Bennett (The Latin Language §48) rejects that lengthening for ascendō, distinguō, suspiciō as “an untenable theory of compensatory lengthening”, and Lewis’s own Elementary Latin Dictionary (1890) prints re-spondeō. Ruling: Macrons are spelling.
  2. 2Write respondeō, restō, respiciō, rescrībō with a short e in the prefix, against Lewis & Short’s rē-. Ruling: re- short before sc, sp, st.
